claim: Hiša Franko is open Wednesday–Sunday only (closed Mon–Tue); dinner runs 19:00–23:00 with last reservation at 20:00.
quote: Dinner Service: 19:00–23:00 (last reservation 20:00) ... Lunch Service: 12:00–16:00 (last reservation 13:00) ... closed Monday and Tuesday

claim: Hiša Franko closes for a full winter break — most recently from early January through mid-February — so winter weekends are off-limits.
quote: Hiša Franko has ended another beautiful season. See you on 14th February 2025

claim: Tolmin Gorges entry is €8 in off-season (Mar–May, Oct–Nov) and €12 in peak (Jun–Sep), with reduced rates for kids and €1 for under-6s and people with disabilities.
quote: Off-Season (March, April, May, October, November): Adults €8.00 ... Peak Season (June, July, August, September): Adults €12.00 ... Children (0-5 years) & people with disabilities: €1.00

claim: Tolmin Gorges operate roughly April through October/early November and are fully closed in winter; peak summer hours run 08:00–19:00.
quote: Tolmin Gorges are usually open from April to October ... During the high season (July to mid September), the Tolmin Gorge is open from 8 a.m. to 7 p.m.

claim: Tolmin Gorges offer wheelchair access only as far as the Devil's Bridge, with dedicated disabled parking near the entrance; the deeper trail has many stairs and is not suitable for strollers or wheelchairs.
quote: Disabled people in wheelchairs and those who find it very difficult to move can go by wheelchair or on foot to the Devil's Bridge ... the path through the Tolmin Gorge is not suitable for strollers

claim: The Kobarid Museum (WWI Isonzo Front) is open year-round but is housed in a protected building without ramps or lifts, so the permanent exhibition is not accessible to visitors with severe mobility impairments.
quote: The museum is not equipped with ramps or an elevator, so the permanent exhibition is not accessible to people with severe mobility handicaps.

claim: Kozjak Waterfall is reachable year-round via a flat 30-minute walk from the Napoleon Bridge car park, with a managed entry (€5) charged only April 2 – October 31; winter visits are at your own risk.
quote: It is possible to visit Kozjak Waterfall all year round ... entrance costs €5.00 per person and is chargeable from the 2nd of April until the 31st of October

claim: The Mangart Saddle toll road (Slovenia's highest asphalt road at 2,072 m) typically opens from the second half of June through end of November, weather-dependent, with a €10 toll per car.
quote: The road usually opens in May and is maintained until the end of November ... road is usually open from the second half of June ... toll at a ticket booth (€10)

claim: Vršič Pass — the high alpine link to Kranjska Gora — is closed to all traffic in winter conditions and typically reopens in late spring once snow clears.
quote: Vršič is the highest mountain pass in Slovenia and is closed to all traffic during winter conditions

claim: Commercial Soča rafting season runs March 26 – October 31, with the biggest water and adrenaline in spring snowmelt and autumn rains; summer water is warmest but still under 16 °C.
quote: Rafting operations are open from March 26th until October 31st ... more abundant with adrenaline in the spring and autumn, when the river has higher water levels

claim: The Kamno–Tolmin kayak section near Kobarid is a class I–II beginner introduction (about 9 km, 3 h total with 1.5 h on water) open to children from age 12.
quote: The Kamno–Tolmin stretch is safe and therefore perfect even for first-time paddlers ... Children from the age of 12 are welcome in the kayak

claim: Public bus links Kobarid with Tolmin (~19 min) and Bovec (~49 min via Tolmin) four times a day on Nomago services; a summer hop-on/hop-off shuttle network around Bovec, Kobarid and Tolmin runs 6 July – 25 August.
quote: From 6 July to 25 August, there are Hop On-Hop Off connections around Bovec and Kobarid, as well as shuttle buses around Tolmin
